label: Approaching (2028–2032 expected)
rationale: No fusion plant has yet delivered sustained electricity to a grid, and engineering breakeven is unproven. 2025 brought record progress (NIF Q=4.13, WEST 22-minute plasma, Helion beginning construction of its Orion plant, CFS raising $863M), with Helion and CFS leading toward 2028-2032 grid timelines if private schedules hold.

label: Distant
rationale: First-of-a-kind fusion plants are projected above $150/MWh, versus $50-78/MWh averages for wind, solar and gas. Nth-of-a-kind plants at $50-100/MWh are plausible only in the 2040s-2050s; all fusion LCOE figures are projections since no plant operates.

label: ⚠️ Mixed
rationale: Renewable generation costs have collapsed (solar LCOE $43/MWh, -90% since 2010), but wholesale prices remain volatile and rose in H1 2025 (EU ~$90/MWh, US ~$48/MWh). Fusion remains commercially unproven, with first plants expected to exceed current nuclear costs.

label: Distant: no fusion LCOE exists (no plant runs); FOAK est. >$150/MWh vs <$100 goal, gas CC ~$78
rationale: No fusion plant produces electricity, so the milestone's own quantity (fusion LCOE) has no measured value and no trend to extrapolate. The only independent estimate (Lindley et al. 2023, legacy) puts first-of-a-kind plants above $150/MWh, against a <$100/MWh goal and a Lazard 2025 gas combined-cycle average of ~$78/MWh; the sole sub-$100 figure is CFS's own nth-of-a-kind projection, which cannot lift a status. Reaching nth-of-a-kind cost needs a fleet built after first plants that proponents themselves target for 2028 to the early 2030s, so there is no evidenced path with an ETA within 10 years: red (Distant).

basis.rule: Milestone red: no evidenced path. There is no measured fusion LCOE (no operating plant) and no trend to extrapolate, and the only sub-$100/MWh figure is a proponent projection (projections never lift a status); ETA >10 years
basis.eta: >10 years (not estimable from evidence: sub-$100/MWh would need nth-of-a-kind plants, which come after first commercial plants that proponents target for 2028 (Helion) to the early 2030s (CFS ARC))
basis.path: None evidenced. Independent FOAK estimate >$150/MWh (Lindley et al. 2023, legacy); CFS NOAK $50-100/MWh is a proponent projection reported by TIME (legacy, non-primary)
blockers: Technical (precursor missing): no fusion device has yet delivered net electricity (Helion missed its 2024 net-electricity target), so no cost data exist
Economic: independent FOAK cost estimate >$150/MWh is above both the $100/MWh goal and gas CC (~$78/MWh avg, Lazard LCOE+ 2025)
basis.benchmark: Goal <$100/MWh ('competitive with gas'); Lazard LCOE+ 2025 gas combined cycle $41-108/MWh, avg ~$78
basis.benchmark_source: README milestone wording; Lazard LCOE+ June 2025 (2025-01-01-lazard-lcoe-2025-rv)
basis.change_note: Rubric correction v1, no new evidence; status stays red, but its grounds are corrected. Under STATUS.md the previous assessment's label ('Distant') gave no level or benchmark. Its rationale also claimed that nth-of-a-kind plants at $50-100/MWh were 'plausible only in the 2040s-2050s' with no evidence record behind that date. It treated a proponent projection (CFS NOAK) as a plausibility signal, and it cited the superseded Lazard record. Red now rests on 'no evidenced path' (no measured fusion LCOE), not on an unsourced roadmap date.

label: Progressing: no fusion power on any grid yet; Helion 2028 ETA is proponent-only, Orion being built
rationale: No fusion plant has delivered electricity to a grid, and no device has yet shown net electricity; Helion missed its own 2024 target. Helion started building its Orion plant in Malaga, WA in July 2025 (reverified from its primary source) and targets delivering power to Microsoft in 2028. CFS targets ARC grid power in the early 2030s; both are funded, but these ETAs are asserted only by the proponents. Green needs a demonstrated precursor at relevant scale and non-proponent corroboration, and neither exists, so this is yellow: a ≤5-year ETA asserted only by the proponent.

basis.rule: Milestone yellow: ETA <=5 years asserted only by the proponent (announced but not achieved). Not green: funded programmes exist, but there is no demonstrated precursor at relevant scale (no net electricity from any device) and no non-proponent corroboration of the ETA
basis.eta: 2028 per Helion (Microsoft PPA; proponent-only); CFS ARC early 2030s (proponent-only); no independent ETA in evidence
basis.path: Helion Orion (D-He3 pulsed FRC, Malaga WA): construction began July 2025, reactor-building permit Oct 2025 (legacy), Polaris prototype operating (legacy), >$1B raised. Backup path: CFS SPARC -> ARC, ~$3B raised
blockers: Technical (precursor missing): no device has demonstrated net electricity; Helion missed its 2024 net-electricity target
Credibility: the only <=5-year ETA comes from the proponent, which has already slipped a prior target
Technical (D-T paths): tritium breeding and neutron-resistant materials remain unproven at scale; ITER D-T operation slipped to 2039
basis.change_note: Rubric correction v1, no new evidence; status stays yellow, but its grounds are corrected. Under STATUS.md the previous label ('Approaching (2028-2032 expected)') used no v1 verdict word. It also presented proponent targets (Helion 2028, CFS early 2030s) as the expected ETA, when they are proponent-only assertions. Its rationale counted plasma-physics records (NIF Q=4.13, WEST 22-min plasma) and funding announcements (CFS $863M, FIA investment) as progress toward grid electricity; they are not the milestone's quantity, and announcements never lift a status. It also cited records since superseded or corrected on reverification (e.g. SPARC 2026 operation was not supported). Yellow now rests only on the proponent-asserted <=5-year ETA, backed by actual Orion construction.
